questions.q: What is the single biggest timing mistake candidates make in a review-board-style presentation, according to this lesson?
options: Spending too long on the opening and prepared walkthrough, leaving too little time for the panel's questions
Spending too much time on the Q&A period and not enough on the prepared walkthrough
Skipping the opening entirely and going straight to Q&A
Presenting the domains in alphabetical order instead of logical order
questions.explain: The questions are where a design actually gets tested, so letting the prepared walkthrough run long and crowd out that time is the mistake this lesson warns against.

questions.q: What is a panel primarily checking for during the opening few minutes of a presentation?
options: Whether the candidate can recite every governor limit from memory
Whether the candidate understood the actual business problem, including its hard facts and key constraints, before presenting the solution
Whether the candidate's slide deck uses the panel's preferred color scheme
Whether the candidate can finish the entire presentation in under two minutes
questions.explain: An opening that jumps straight to a diagram without restating the problem reads as having skipped understanding it, even if the design itself is sound — which is exactly what the panel is listening for.

questions.q: Why do the strongest domain-by-domain walkthroughs present data, security, and integration architecture as one connected story rather than three separate topics?
options: Because Salesforce certification rules require exactly three domains per presentation
Because panels only ever ask about one domain at a time
Because each domain's choice in a good design follows from and reinforces the others, and presenting them as disconnected topics loses that coherence
Because separating domains makes a presentation easier to time correctly
questions.explain: Using Meridian Outfitters as the example, the unified customer-profile layer, the event-driven sync, and the no-merge decision all reinforce each other — that connectedness is what a strong walkthrough communicates.

questions.q: What are the two things the strongest answers do, in order, when fielding a panel question?
options: Re-present the entire solution from scratch, then ask the panel to repeat the question
Deflect the question, then change the subject to a stronger part of the design
Ask the panel a clarifying question before saying anything substantive
Directly answer the specific question asked, then briefly justify the reasoning behind that answer
questions.explain: A common failure mode is treating every question as an invitation to re-present the whole solution; the better instinct is answering precisely what was asked, then justifying it briefly, leaving room for a follow-up.

questions.q: In the recommended solo mock-session exercise, what should the predicted panel questions be drawn from?
options: A generic list of Salesforce trivia questions unrelated to the chosen case study
The chosen case study's own specific edge cases and scenario details
Whatever topic the candidate feels most comfortable discussing
Questions about a completely different case study than the one presented
questions.explain: The exercise asks you to predict questions grounded in the specific scenario you presented, mirroring how a real panel probes the actual design in front of them rather than generic trivia.
